comments.body:
⚠️ severity: IMPORTANT —
⚠️ **IMPORTANT: docs/ci.md contradicts the implemented lookup-failure behavior**

`docs/ci.md:266` states the artefact-cache class is "kept on ANY ticket-state
lookup failure (never delete blind)". The implemented — and tested — behavior
is narrower: a lookup failure blocks only the **early** reclaim; a stale (>24h)
cache is still deleted by the 24h backstop:

```bash
# scripts/sweep_stale_drafts.sh:241-245
elif [ "$stale" = "true" ]; then
  gh api -X DELETE "repos/$repo/releases/$id" >/dev/null
```

Everything else in the PR states the carve-out; this sentence is the outlier:

- the script's own header (sweep_stale_drafts.sh:47-48): "KEPT on any
  ticket-state lookup failure (never delete blind) — **only the 24h backstop
  then applies**";
- the PR description's own Test Coverage bullet: "24h backstop for
  **open/unknown** state";
- the `art-backstop-unknown-stale` test, which asserts the DELETE fires and
  reasons "it only blocks the early reclaim".

An auditor tracing a deleted state-unknown cache would read docs/ci.md as a
promise of keep — and conclude the sweeper misbehaved, when in fact it did
exactly what the header/tests specify.

Two prose strings repeat the same misstatement by describing the swept cohort
as "ticket still open" when it also includes state-UNKNOWN drafts:

- `scripts/sweep_stale_drafts.sh:244` — "swept after 24h with the ticket still
  open (parked leg …)" — fires for lookup failures too;
- `scripts/sweep_stale_drafts.sh:412` — "swept after 24h when the ticket stays
  open".

Fix (one lap, doc-only + two prose strings): reword docs/ci.md:266 to
"kept on any ticket-state lookup failure — only the 24h backstop then applies"
(mirroring the script header), and make both prose strings say "with the
ticket still open **or its state unknown**".

comments.author: ai-teammate
comments.body:
💡 severity: SUGGESTION —
💡 **SUGGESTION: the gh stub's permission model doesn't cover the new issues lookup**

The stub maps every `api` call to `need=contents`
(`test/release_hygiene_test_support.dart:536` — pre-existing line), so the new
per-ticket cycle-state lookup `gh api "repos/$repo/issues/$num"`
(`scripts/sweep_stale_drafts.sh:234`) passes permission enforcement in tests
even though in production it needs the `issues` scope. The PR Notes say the
call is "covered by the job's existing `issues: write` grant", and
docs/ci.md's stub rationale (review of #294) is explicitly "a dropped grant
fails CI instead of silently degrading" — but for **this** call a dropped
`issues:` grant stays green: the stub serves the fixture regardless of the
granted scopes, while production 403s every lookup, `state` stays empty, and
the early reclaim dies silently (the 24h backstop survives, so nothing breaks
loudly — the feature just stops working with no test signal).

Mirror the #294 precedent this stub comment cites — refine the need-case so
`api repos/*/issues/<n>` requires `issues`:

```bash
case "\$cmd \$2" in
  "run list"|"run view"|"run watch"|"run rerun") need=actions ;;
  "issue "*|"label "*) need=issues ;;
  "release "*) need=contents ;;
esac
# gh api: scope follows the resource path (gh-236 lookup = issues:read)
[ "\$cmd" = "api" ] && case "\$2" in
  */issues/*) need=issues ;;
  *) need=contents ;;
esac
```

Suggestion-level: the `issues` grant as a whole is still pinned indirectly —
the auto-close test (`issue close`) 403s without it — so nothing blocks merge
here; this just closes the residual silent-degradation window on the new call.

## Fixed — docs + prose now state the carve-out exactly as implemented

Agreed — the sentence was the outlier: every other artifact (script header, PR description, `art-backstop-unknown-stale` test) states that a lookup failure blocks only the **early** reclaim, while `docs/ci.md` promised an unqualified keep. Fixed in one lap, exactly along the suggested wording:

**`docs/ci.md:266-267`** — reworded to mirror the script header verbatim:

> kept on any ticket-state lookup failure (never delete blind) — only the 24h backstop then applies.

**`scripts/sweep_stale_drafts.sh:244`** — swept-cohort prose now reads "swept after 24h with the ticket still open **or its state unknown** (parked leg …)".

**`scripts/sweep_stale_drafts.sh:412`** — E1-footer prose now reads "swept after 24h when the ticket stays open **or its state is unknown**".

Behavior unchanged — the fixes are doc/prose-only, per the thread's fix plan.

**TDD pinning** (so the contradiction cannot regress):

- `test/release_artifact_draft_lifecycle_test.dart:362` — `the 24h-backstop prose names the swept cohort truthfully …` runs a stale state-unknown cache (`ai-gh-2208`, no state fixture) plus a stale `ai-pr-210` and a kept human draft, asserts both prose strings carry the carve-out **and** that both unknown-state caches are still DELETEd by the backstop (behavior preserved). RED before the fix: both prose assertions failed against the old wording.
- `test/release_artifact_draft_lifecycle_test.dart:424` — `docs/ci.md states the lookup-failure carve-out exactly as implemented` asserts the doc sentence contains the carve-out and the old unqualified "kept on ANY ticket-state lookup failure" claim is gone (whitespace-normalized match, robust to reflow). RED before the fix.

Commits: `84e7ed50fb` (docs + script prose), `10e48cd1a9` + `b6b9036b8f` (tests, format). All 12 tests in `release_artifact_draft_lifecycle_test.dart` and the full release-hygiene suites pass.

comments.author: ai-teammate
comments.body:
## Fixed — the stub's permission model now covers the issues lookup

Picked up this lap (cheap, and it closes the exact silent-degradation window the finding describes). `test/release_hygiene_test_support.dart:536-549` — the blanket `"release "*|"api"*) need=contents` mapping is refined so the scope follows the resource path, per the #294 precedent the stub comment cites:

```bash
if [ "\$cmd" = "api" ]; then
  case "\$2" in
    */issues/*) need=issues ;;
    *) need=contents ;;
  esac
fi
```

- `api repos/<o>/<r>/issues/<n>` (the gh-236 cycle-state lookup, `sweep_stale_drafts.sh:234`) now requires `issues`; a dropped `issues:` grant 403s in tests — and since every `runSweeper` run enforces the real `sweep-drafts` grant via `sweepPermissions()`, dropping `issues: write` from `daily-publish.yml` now fails the lifecycle suite loudly instead of silently dead-ing the early reclaim.
- The release paths are untouched: `api --paginate repos/…/releases` and `api -X DELETE repos/…/releases/<id>` keep `need=contents` (deleting draft releases is the contents grant), pinned by the same test.
- One wrinkle handled: the script swallows lookup stderr (`2>/dev/null`), so the 403 alone is not visible end-to-end — the fail-safe keep still hides it. That is why the new test pins the permission model directly (stub-invoked probe) **and** behaviorally:

**`test/release_artifact_draft_lifecycle_test.dart:456`** — `the gh stub requires the issues scope for api .../issues/<n> …`:
1. invokes the stub with `GH_STUB_PERMISSIONS: contents` and `api repos/OWNER/REPO/issues/228` → expects exit 1 and stderr naming `needs 'issues'` (RED before the fix: the old mapping served the fixture and exited 0);
2. asserts the releases DELETE path stays contents-green;
3. end-to-end `runSweeper` with only `contents` granted on a closed-cycle fresh cache → lookup 403 → state unknown → fail-safe keep, no reclaim, sweep stays green (`runSweeper` gained an `extraEnv` parameter, mirroring the existing `runTrainGuard` pattern).

Commits: `10e48cd1a9` + `b6b9036b8f`. Full release suites (hygiene, stale-draft reclaim, asset gate, publish immutability, artefact-cache lifecycle — every consumer of this stub) pass; `dart analyze` clean.

## Automated Code Review — REQUEST_CHANGES

**Summary**: The gh-236 artefact-cache lifecycle is well-built and correctly pinned (9 new + 125 regression tests green, shellcheck clean) — one docs-vs-behavior contradiction must be fixed first: `docs/ci.md` promises "kept on ANY ticket-state lookup failure", while the sweeper sweeps unknown-state caches after 24h (per its own header, the PR description, and the `art-backstop-unknown-stale` test).

**Key Issues**:
- ⚠️ `docs/ci.md:266` — lookup-failure clause mistates the behavior; same wrong "ticket still open" prose in `scripts/sweep_stale_drafts.sh:244` and `:412`.

**Next Steps**:
1. Reword `docs/ci.md:266` to mirror the script header ("only the 24h backstop then applies"); fix both prose strings to say "still open or state unknown".
2. Optional: gh stub's permission model should require `issues` scope for `api .../issues/<n>` (inline suggestion).

**Digest**: `scripts/sweep_stale_drafts.sh:248` — `art_kept_tags` accumulates but is never read; print it or drop it. · `scripts/sweep_stale_drafts.sh:164` — the `ai-(gh|pr)` guard hardcodes gh/pr key shapes; a future factory key (e.g. ADO `ai-ado-<n>`) silently falls back to the bot bucket and resurrects the recurring-issue bug for that shape.
